newsitem.title: UK: High sulph barges bid up, crude supports Euro swap.
newsitem.headline: High sulph barges bid up, crude supports Euro swap.

text.p: NWE fuel oil barges jumped $2 on Tuesday as Brent's firmness brought a bit of bullishness back to the market, though doubts lingered as to how long it would last, traders said.
High sulphur barge prices were bid up for the second day by one or two dealers, with deals done at $85, $86, $86.50 and $87 fob ARA.
But offers later sank back to $86 and met with very poor buying interest.
"We're still looking for other buyers to confirm that numbers really are at the higher level," said one trader.
The better physical and swaps level lent some support to cargoes but they were very thinly talked and failed to move.
Low sulphur was also supported by better swaps, which had been boosted by crude's pick-up, but numbers remained level.
"The swap's trend is a bit firmer but I don't think it's that way on the physical and I don't think it will last," said one trader.
"People think Europe is one of the cheapest swaps markets and that has brought people in to buy," he added.
Straight-run was mildly firmer with buying interest stretching into May, mainly for material to take trans-Atlantic.
